t: From stem cell to fertilizing sperm
q: Put the events in a sperm's life in order, from the stem cell on the basement membrane to a sperm able to fertilize an egg.
key: The order follows both the sperm's route and its maturation: mitosis, meiosis I and II, remodeling, release, transit through the ducts, epididymal motility, ejaculation and finally capacitation in the female tract; the testis builds the sperm, the epididymis makes it move and the female tract makes it fertile.
items: Spermatogonia divide by mitosis on the basement membrane
Diploid stem cells must renew themselves and send committed daughters inward before any meiosis can happen, so this mitotic step comes first.
Primary spermatocytes replicate DNA and complete meiosis I
Committed cells cross the Sertoli tight junctions, copy their DNA and divide to give haploid secondary spermatocytes, so meiosis I precedes meiosis II.
Secondary spermatocytes complete meiosis II to form haploid spermatids
The second division follows within hours and splits the sister chromatids, leaving round haploid spermatids that no longer divide.
Spermatids remodel in spermiogenesis: acrosome, flagellum, shed cytoplasm
Without dividing, each spermatid builds its acrosome from the Golgi, grows a tail and sheds cytoplasm, so shape change comes only after meiosis ends.
Spermiation releases immotile sperm into the tubule lumen
Remodeled sperm are freed into the tubule fluid only once their shape is complete, and they are still unable to swim.
Sperm pass through the rete testis and efferent ductules
Tubular fluid carries immotile sperm out of the testis, and the ductules reabsorb most of the fluid before the sperm reach the epididymis.
Sperm gain motility and are stored in the epididymis
Transit through the epididymal head and body gives forward motility, and the tail stores the sperm until ejaculation.
Emission and ejaculation carry sperm through the ductus deferens to the urethra
Sympathetic emission moves sperm and gland fluids into the urethra before pudendal-driven contractions expel the semen.
Capacitation and the acrosome reaction occur in the female tract
Only after ejaculation do female tract secretions make sperm able to fertilize, so these steps cannot occur in the testis or epididymis.
